Market Opportunity
paragraphs: AVITA Medical is a leading therapeutic acute wound care company delivering transformative solutions designed to optimize wound healing, accelerate patient recovery, and improve clinical and economic outcomes across the continuum of acute wound management. Our technologies address critical healing needs arising from burns, traumatic injuries and surgical repairs, through a portfolio of proprietary and complementary products that support wound bed preparation, definitive closure, and recovery.

Our current commercial portfolio includes RECELL® ("RECELL"), and two complementary wound care products, PermeaDerm® and Cohealyx, which together support a comprehensive standard of care for acute wounds.

At the forefront of our portfolio is RECELL, approved by the United States Food & Drug Administration (the "FDA") for the treatment of thermal burn wounds and full-thickness skin defects. While RECELL is also approved in the United States for restoring pigmentation of stable depigmented vitiligo lesions, we have paused further commercial investment in vitiligo at this time.

In 2024 and 2025, we expanded our product offerings to address additional acute wound care needs. In January 2024, we entered into an exclusive multi-year distribution agreement with Stedical Scientific, Inc. ("Stedical") to market, sell, and distribute PermeaDerm, a biosynthetic wound matrix in the United States ("U.S."). In March 2025, we entered into a multi-year agreement to also manufacture PermeaDerm. In July 2024, we entered into an exclusive multi-year development and distribution agreement with Collagen Matrix, LLC d/b/a as Regenity Biosciences ("Regenity"), granting us exclusive rights to market, sell, and distribute Cohealyx, an AVITA-medical branded collagen-based dermal matrix in the U.S., with potential expansion into the European Union ("E.U."), Australia, and Japan. Cohealyx was commercially launched in the U.S. on April 1, 2025.

AVITA Medical Limited ("AVITA Australia"), the former Australian parent company of AVITA Medical, was founded in December 1992. On October 1, 2019, AVITA Australia began trading its American Depositary Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market ("Nasdaq") under the symbol "RCEL". In 2020, the Company redomiciled to the U.S. (the "Redomiciliation"). Today, our common stock continues to trade on Nasdaq under "RCEL" and our CHESS Depositary Interests ("CDIs") trade on the Australian Securities Exchange ("ASX") under the symbol "AVH."

RECELL remains the cornerstone of our business; however, beginning in 2024 we evolved AVITA Medical into a multi-product acute wound care platform company. Our strategy is to build a comprehensive portfolio that addresses wound management from initial coverage and wound bed preparation through definitive closure and healing, while leveraging a single commercial infrastructure focused on burn, trauma and surgical centers.
• Increasing market penetration in U.S. burn centers, positioning RECELL as the standard of care in burn management;
• Expanding adoption of RECELL for the treatment of traumatic and surgical wounds throughout the U.S.;
• Commercializing and expanding adoption of Cohealyx as a dermal matrix that supports wound bed preparation and accelerates readiness for grafting;
• Driving adoption of RECELL GO mini in burn and trauma centers treating smaller wounds;
• Advancing post-market clinical studies for Cohealyx and PermeaDerm to generate additional clinical and health economic evidence supporting adoption;
• Expanding internationally through distributor-led commercialization following regulatory approvals, including CE Mark approval for RECELL GO in Europe;
• Driving commercial revenue growth, improving operating leverage, generating positive cash flow, and achieving long-term operating profitability; and
• Pursuing additional business development opportunities complementary to our target acute wound care markets.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business Operations
We have experienced significant losses, expect losses to continue for the foreseeable future and may never achieve or maintain profitability.

Servicing our debt requires a significant amount of cash and we are subject to a number of restrictive covenants relating to our indebtedness, which may restrict our business and financing activities.
The markets in which we operate are highly competitive and innovative. Our competitors may develop products that render our products less attractive or obsolete and our business may deteriorate.
Our success depends, in part, on our relationships with, and the efforts of, third-party distributors.
Certain of our products are dependent on specialized sources of supply potentially subject to disruption which could have a material, adverse impact on our business.

Our business, results of operations, and financial condition could be materially and adversely affected by any of these risks, and in such event, the trading price of our common stock would likely decline, and you might lose all or part of your investment. This Annual Report also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties, and our results could materially differ from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements. See "Forward-Looking Statements" included elsewhere within this Annual Report for a discussion of certain risks, uncertainties and assumptions associated with these statements.

Although we have begun full scale marketing and sales of our products in the United States and other jurisdictions, we have not yet achieved profitability. We had a total net loss of $48.6 million and $61.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. We have incurred a cumulative deficit of $408.4 million through December 31, 2025. We anticipate that we may continue to incur losses at least until sales of our products are adequate to fund operating expenses. We may not be able to successfully achieve or sustain profitability. Successful transition to profitable operations is dependent upon achieving a level of revenues adequate to support our cost structure, including in new markets where regulatory approval is in process or pending.

We had previously entered into a credit agreement with OrbiMed Advisors, LLC (as amended, the "Previous Credit Agreement") on October 18, 2023, most recently amended in the Previous Credit Agreement's Sixth Amendment, on November 5, 2025 (the "Sixth Amendment") and incurred $40.0 million of indebtedness secured by substantially all of our assets.

On January 13, 2026, we entered into a new Credit Agreement and Guaranty (the "Perceptive Credit Agreement"), and Security Agreement (the "Security Agreement"), by and among us, as borrower, Avita Medical Americas, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, as guarantor (the "Guarantor," taken together with the Company, the "Obligors") and Perceptive Credit Holdings V, LP as a lender and the administrative agent (the "Lender," and the "Administrative Agent," as applicable). The Perceptive Credit Agreement provides for a five-year senior secured credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $60 million (the "Loan Facility"), of which (i) $50 million was funded on the Closing Date (the "Initial Commitment Amount") and (ii) $10 million will be made available, at our discretion by notice to the Administrative Agent on or before March 31, 2027, subject to satisfaction of a certain net revenue requirement (the "Additional Commitment Amount"). On the Closing Date, we closed on the Initial Commitment Amount, less certain fees and expenses payable to or on behalf of the Lender. Simultaneously with the closing of the Initial Commitment Amount, we repaid in full and terminated all of obligations and commitments (other than previously issued warrants) (the "Refinancing Transaction")[1] under the Previous Credit Agreement.

This level of debt could have significant consequences on future operations, including increasing our vulnerability to adverse economic and industry conditions and limiting our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business and the markets in which we compete.

Our ability to make scheduled payments of interest depends on our future performance, which is subject to interest rate risk, as well as economic, financial, competitive, and other factors beyond our control. We are exposed to risks related to a potential rising interest rate environment for the debt, which could cause our borrowing costs to rise and impact our liquidity. Our business may not generate cash flow from operations in the future sufficient to service our debt in cash while simultaneously making necessary capital expenditures. In addition, if the Company's net revenue does not equal or exceed a certain amount for upcoming fiscal periods as set forth in the Perceptive Credit Agreement, then the Company will be in default of the Perceptive Credit Agreement.

paragraphs: On January 13, 2026, we closed a five-year credit facility providing up to $60 million in capital with a new lender and refinanced our existing debt, receiving total net proceeds of $6.0 million after repayment of our existing debt and certain fees. As part of the new credit facility, we established trailing twelve-month ("TTM") revenue covenants aligned with our current operating trajectory. The initial TTM revenue covenant is $68.5 million for the first quarter ending March 31, 2026, and $73 million for the full year 2026. For additional information, see Liquidity and Capital Resources below.

On January 5, 2026, the Board of Directors recognized the contributions of long-time Director (and former Chair of the Board) Lou Panaccio, whose last day of service was December 31, 2025. Following Mr. Panaccio's retirement, the Board was pleased to announce Joe Woody's appointment as a new Director pursuant to an offer letter to join the Board as of January 1, 2026.

On October 16, 2025, Mr. Vance, the Chair of the Board of Directors, assumed the position of Interim Chief Executive Officer (the "Interim CEO") upon the departure of Mr. Corbett from the Company and the Board.

On October 1, 2025, the CMS approved a New Technology Add-On Payment ("NTAP") for the RECELL® System, applicable to acute non-thermal full-thickness skin defects—such as traumatic injuries and surgical wounds—that require inpatient care and are treated with RECELL in combination with a meshed autograft. This NTAP designation allows Medicare Part A inpatient claims to receive up to $4,875 in additional reimbursement per case, beyond the standard MS-DRG base rate, provided CMS thresholds and coding criteria are met. The NTAP is effective from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, and was granted under CMS's alternative pathway recognizing RECELL's FDA Breakthrough Device status, reinforcing its clinical value and supporting broader hospital adoption.

On September 14, 2025, we obtained the CE Mark for RECELL GO under the European Union Medical Device Regulation ("EU MDR"). This allows us to commercialize RECELL GO in Europe and other markets that recognize the CE Mark.

During 2025, we continued to expand the clinical and real-world evidence supporting RECELL and its acute wound care portfolio, with an emphasis on hospital utilization, wound closure outcomes and staged care pathways. Data presented at major burn and wound care conferences highlighted reproducible outcomes in clinical practice and increasing surgeon adoption across diverse patient populations.
Key studies presented during 2025 included the following:

• Real-world hospital length of stay ("LOS") analysis: A registry-based analysis of 741 matched adult patients with deep partial-thickness burns from the American Burn Association's Burn Care Quality Platform compared RECELL with split-thickness skin grafting. The study demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in hospital length of stay of approximately 5.6 days, or 36%, for RECELL-treated patients, with consistent reductions across burn size subgroups up to 30% TBSA. RECELL-treated patients were more likely to be discharged directly home, supporting conclusions of improved recovery trajectories and hospital throughput.

• Global systematic review of RECELL clinical evidence: A systematic review of 99 peer-reviewed studies, including 27 comparative analyses and more than 8,000 patients, found that RECELL consistently reduced donor site burden, achieved healing times comparable to or faster than conventional grafting, and demonstrated favorable pain, aesthetic and health economic outcomes across wound types. The authors concluded that the consistency and breadth of evidence support RECELL as an emerging standard of care in wound closure across diverse populations and care settings.

• Accelerated wound bed preparation with Cohealyx: A June 2025 clinical publication evaluating Cohealyx reported rapid wound bed vascularization and readiness for autografting within approximately 5 to 10 days in a case series of complex full-thickness wounds, compared with the 2-to-4-week timelines typically reported for conventional dermal matrices. This data confirms previously published pre-clinical work. Investigators concluded that earlier readiness for definitive closure may reduce patient burden and complication risk.

• Temporary wound coverage using PermeaDerm: In a retrospective case series, PermeaDerm was used to temporize mixed-depth and full-thickness burn wounds in patients unable to undergo immediate autografting. Surgeons cited ease of application, reduced operative complexity relative to cadaveric allograft, and the advantage of maintaining direct visualization of the wound bed. The study concluded that PermeaDerm provided safe and effective temporary coverage prior to definitive wound closure.
Sources for the studies referenced above were provided in the relevant press releases we issued from June through November 2025.

In 2025, we initiated two post-market clinical trials, PermeaDerm I and Cohealyx I, to further evaluate the performance of our technologies in the treatment of acute and complex wounds. The PermeaDerm I study is designed to assess cost and clinical outcomes when used as a temporizing treatment, and enrollment in this study has surpassed 75%. The Cohealyx I study is intended to evaluate time to autografting compared to a literature derived performance goal, with enrollment completed we expect data in 2026.

In early 2026, presentations at the Boswick Burn & Wound Symposium extended this evidence to staged wound care strategies, including surgeon-reported cases integrating RECELL, PermeaDerm and Cohealyx on the same patient. Together, these data reflect growing use of AVITA Medical's integrated portfolio across wound coverage, preparation and definitive closure.

paragraphs: AVITA Medical 是一家領先的急性傷口照護治療公司，提供創新解決方案，用以優化傷口癒合、加速病患復原，並改善急性傷口管理全過程的臨牀與經濟成果。我們的技術解決因燒傷、外傷及手術修復所產生的關鍵癒合需求，透過一組專屬且互補的產品組合，支持傷口牀準備、最終閉合及復原。
我們目前的商業產品組合包括 RECELL® ("RECELL"), 以及兩種互補的傷口照護產品 PermeaDerm® 和 Cohealyx，這些產品共同支持急性傷口的完整照護標準。
我們產品組合的重點為 RECELL，已獲得美國食品藥物管理局 (the "FDA") 批准用以治療熱力燒傷傷口及全層皮膚缺損。雖然 RECELL 也已獲得美國批准用以恢復穩定脫色素白癜風病竈的色素，但我們目前暫時停止對白癜風的進一步商業投資。

在 2024 年及 2025 年，我們擴充了產品組合，以應對更多急性傷口照護需求。2024 年 1 月，我們與 Stedical Scientific, Inc. ("Stedical") 籤訂獨家多年分銷協議，用以在美國 ("U.S.") 市場行銷、銷售及分銷 PermeaDerm，這是一款生物合成傷口基質。2025 年 3 月，我們簽訂多年協議，也開始製造 PermeaDerm。2024 年 7 月，我們與 Collagen Matrix, LLC d/b/a as Regenity Biosciences ("Regenity") 籤訂獨家多年開發與分銷協議，授予我們獨家權利在美國 ("U.S.") 市場行銷、銷售及分銷 Cohealyx，這是一款 AVITA-medical 品牌的膠原蛋白基質產品，未來有潛力拓展至歐盟 ("E.U.")、澳洲及日本。Cohealyx 於 2025 年 4 月 1 日在美國正式上市。

AVITA Medical Limited ("AVITA Australia")，即 AVITA Medical 的前澳洲母公司，於 1992 年 12 月成立。2019 年 10 月 1 日，AVITA Australia 開始在納斯達克資本市場 ("Nasdaq") 交易其美國存託股，代號為 "RCEL"。2020 年，本公司進行美國註冊 (the "Redomiciliation")。目前，我們的普通股繼續在納斯達克交易，代號為 "RCEL"，而我們的 CHESS 存託憑證 ("CDIs") 則在澳洲證券交易所 ("ASX") 交易，代號為 "AVH."
RECELL 備受我們業務的重視；然而，自 2024 年起，我們將 AVITA Medical 轉型為一家多產品的急性傷口照護平台公司。我們的策略是建立一個完整的產品組合，從傷口初期覆蓋及傷口牀準備，一直到最終閉合及癒合，同時利用一個專注於燒傷、外傷及手術中心的單一商業基礎設施。
• 提升美國燒傷中心的市場佔有率，將 RECELL 定位為燒傷管理的標準照護方案；
• 擴展 RECELL 在美國用以治療外傷及手術傷口的應用範圍。
• 將 Cohealyx 商品化並擴大其作為皮膚基質的應用，用以支持創傷牀準備及加速移植準備;
• 推動 RECELL GO mini 在處理較小創傷的燒傷與創傷中心的採用;
• 推進 Cohealyx 與 PermeaDerm 的上市後臨牀研究，以產生額外的臨牀與衛生經濟證據，支持其採用;
• 透過經認證的經銷商領導的商業化方式，於取得法規批准後擴大國際業務，包括在歐洲取得 RECELL GO 的 CE Mark 許可;
• 推動商業收入成長、提高營運槓桿效益、產生正向現金流，並實現長期營運獲利能力; 和
• 追求與目標急性創傷照護市場相輔相成的額外業務發展機會。

paragraphs: 於 2026 年 1 月 13 日，本公司與新貸款人簽訂五年期信用融資協議，提供最高 60 百萬美元資本，並重新融資現有債務，獲得淨資金 6.0 百萬美元，扣除現有債務償還及某些費用後。根據新信用融資協議，本公司設定了十二個月營業收入（"TTM"）約束條件，與本公司現有營運路徑一致。第一季截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日的初始 TTM 營業收入約束條件為 68.5 百萬美元，2026 年全年為 73 百萬美元。如需更多資訊，請參閱下文「流動性及資本資源」部分。
於 2026 年 1 月 5 日，董事會認可長期董事（並曾任董事會主席）Lou Panaccio 的貢獻，其最後服務日為 2025 年 12 月 31 日。在 Panaccio 先生退休後，董事會樂意宣佈 Joe Woody 先生根據加入董事會的聘書，自 2026 年 1 月 1 日起擔任新董事。
於 2025 年 10 月 16 日，Vance 先生，董事會主席，在 Corbett 先生離開本公司及董事會後，擔任臨時首席執行官（"Interim CEO"）。

於 2025 年 10 月 1 日，CMS 批准 RECELL® 系統的新型技術附加支付（"NTAP"），適用於需住院治療的急性非熱性全層皮膚缺損—例如外傷及手術傷口—並與網格自體移植物結合治療。此 NTAP 設定允許 Medicare Part A 住院申報案件，每案可獲得最高 4,875 美元的額外補償，超過標準 MS-DRG 基準率，前提是符合 CMS 門檻及編碼標準。NTAP 有效期間為 2025 年 10 月 1 日至 2026 年 9 月 30 日，並根據 CMS 的替代途徑授予，認可 RECELL 的 FDA 突破性裝置地位，強化其臨牀價值並支持更廣泛的醫院採用。
於 2025 年 9 月 14 日，本公司取得 RECELL GO 的 CE 證明，根據歐盟醫療器材法規（"EU MDR"）。此證明允許本公司在歐洲及其他承認 CE 證明的市場推廣 RECELL GO。
2025 年期間，本公司持續擴展支持 RECELL 及其急性傷口照護產品組合的臨牀及實際應用證據，重點在於醫院使用率、傷口閉合結果及分階段照護路徑。在主要燒傷及傷口照護會議上展示的資料強調了臨牀實踐中可重複的結果，以及在多樣化患者羣體中外科醫生的採用率增加。
2025 年期間提出的關鍵研究包括以下內容：

• 實際醫院住院天數（"LOS"）分析：根據美國燒傷協會的燒傷照護品質平台，一項基於登記資料的分析比較 741 名匹配成人患者的深層部分厚度燒傷， RECELL 與分層皮膚移植的結果。該研究顯示 RECELL 治療患者的住院天數顯著減少約 5.6 天，或 36%，在不同燒傷面積子羣組中均有約 30% TBSA 的一致減少。RECELL 治療患者更可能直接出院回家，支持改善復原路徑及醫院運作效率的結論。

• 全球系統性審視 RECELL 臨牀證據：系統性審視 99 篇同儕評審研究，包括 27 篇比較分析及超過 8,000 名病患，發現 RECELL 一致降低供體部位負擔，達成與傳統植皮技術相當或更快的癒合時間，並在不同類型傷口中顯示出良好的疼痛、外觀及健康經濟結果。作者結論指出，證據的一致性與廣度支持 RECELL 為傷口閉合的 emerging standard of care（新興標準照護）於多樣族羣與照護環境中。
• 使用 Cohealyx 加速傷口牀準備：2025 年 6 月臨牀出版物評估 Cohealyx，報告在複雜全層傷口的案例系列中，約 5 到 10 天內即達成傷口牀血管化與自體植皮準備，與傳統真皮矩陣通常報導的 2 到 4 週時間相比顯著縮短。此數據確認先前發表的預臨牀研究。研究人員結論指出，較早的準備可能降低病患負擔與並發症風險。
• 使用 PermeaDerm 進行暫時傷口覆蓋：在回溯性案例系列中，PermeaDerm 用於暫時覆蓋無法立即進行自體植皮的混合深度與全層燒傷傷口。外科醫師提及應用簡易、相較於捐贈體異體植皮減少手術複雜度，以及維持傷口牀直接視覺化的優勢。該研究結論指出，PermeaDerm 提供安全有效的暫時覆蓋，以待最終傷口閉合。
上述研究的來源資訊已於 2025 年 6 月至 11 月期間發佈的相關新聞稿中提供。
2025 年，我們啟動兩項上市後臨牀試驗，PermeaDerm I 與 Cohealyx I，以進一步評估我們技術在治療急性與複雜傷口的表現。PermeaDerm I 試驗設計用以評估作為暫時治療時的成本與臨牀結果，且此試驗的參與人數已超過 75%。Cohealyx I 試驗旨在評估自體植皮時間與文獻導出的表現目標相比，預期於 2026 年取得數據。
2026 年初，於 Boswick 燒傷與傷口學會的演講中，這些證據被擴展至分階段傷口照護策略，包括外科醫師報導的整合 RECELL、PermeaDerm 與 Cohealyx 同一病患的案例。這些數據反映 AVITA Medical 整合產品組合在傷口覆蓋、準備與最終閉合的應用日益增加。

headings: 與我們業務運作相關的風險
我們已歷經重大虧損，預期虧損將持續一段可預見的時間，並可能永遠無法達成或維持獲利。
服務我們的債務需要大量現金，我們受到與債務相關的若干限制性契約約束，這些契約可能限制我們的業務與融資活動。
我們所處的市場具有高度競爭與創新性。我們的競爭對手可能開發出產品，使我們的產品變得較不具吸引力或過時，進而使我們的業務惡化。
我們的成功在一定程度上取決於第三方經銷商的關係及其努力。
我們的部分產品依賴特殊的供應來源，這些來源可能受到幹擾，進而對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
我們可能面臨進一步臨牀研究的顯著延誤，這些研究是支持對我們技術的其他商業應用的監管申請所必需的。
產品開發是一項費用高昂、不確定且耗時的過程。
產品之研發與商業化需要成功完成監管審批程序，且可能遭遇延誤或失敗。
本公司高度依賴美國之監管審批，未能維持該審批將對本公司業務與前景造成重大影響。
在某一管轄區取得並維持產品之監管審批，並不表示本公司將能在其他管轄區成功取得該產品之監管審批。
因未預見事件所導致之產品回收或存貨損失，可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司面臨製造風險，可能影響本公司製造產品之能力，並可能降低本公司毛利率，對業務與營運成果造成負面影響。
遵守環境、健康與安全要求成本高昂，若未能達成，可能導致重大財務罰款、高昂訴訟費用，並對業務造成重大不利影響。
若美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）認為本公司已行銷或推廣產品用於未經核准之用途，本公司可能面臨民事罰款及/或刑事處罰。
本公司依賴資訊科技系統執行關鍵業務功能，並維持業務運作。
網路安全事件可能幹擾本公司業務，危害機密資料，造成聲譽損害，並使本公司面臨訴訟及聯邦與州政府調查。
關稅與貿易政策變動可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
與產業及科技相關的風險
本公司可能在全世界保護智慧財產權之權利上遇到困難。
本公司可能因涉及專利及其他智慧財產權之權利爭議或訴訟而產生重大成本，且可能無法保護本公司對技術之權利或使用權。
本公司可能因產品責任訴訟而面臨耗時且成本高昂的法律程序及重大負債。
本公司可能因不利的價格規範或第三方覆蓋範圍及賠償政策，而無法成功商業化現有產品或其他未來產品。
總體經濟及社會風險
總體經濟條件惡化或對未來經濟條件的不確定性，可能會對本公司造成不利影響。
與本公司普通股及 CDIs 有關的風險
本公司普通股及 CDIs 所在市場的交易量相對有限，且未來是否能發展出更活躍、更具流動性的交易市場，仍存在不確定性。
本公司普通股及 CDIs 的市場價格及交易量可能波動，且可能受到變動性影響
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨重大風險。您應仔細審閱本年度報告中所列的所有資訊，包括下列風險因素。本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況可能因任何這些風險而受到重大且不利的影響，若發生此情況，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本年度報告亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述，本公司結果可能與這些展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異。請參閱本年度報告其他處所附的「展望性陳述」，以瞭解與這些陳述相關的某些風險、不確定性及假設。
本公司先前已與OrbiMed Advisors, LLC（經修正後，稱為「先前信貸協議」）於2023年10月18日簽訂信貸協議，最近一次修正為「先前信貸協議」的第六次修正案，於2025年11月5日（稱為「第六次修正案」），並負擔40.0 百萬美元的債務，以本公司 substantially all 的資產為擔保。

本公司於2026年1月13日與Perceptive Credit Holdings V, LP 等簽訂新信貸協議及擔保協議（稱為「Perceptive 信貸協議」），以及擔保協議（稱為「擔保協議」），由本公司作為借款人，Avita Medical Americas, LLC，本公司之 wholly-owned 子公司作為擔保人（稱為「擔保人」，與本公司合稱為「負債人」），以及Perceptive Credit Holdings V, LP 為貸款人及行政代理（稱為「貸款人」及「行政代理」，視情況而定）。Perceptive 信貸協議提供一個五年期的高級 secured 信貸設施，總本金金額最高為60 百萬美元（稱為「貸款設施」），其中（i）50 百萬美元於關閉日（稱為「初始承諾金額」）已撥款，以及（ii）10 百萬美元將根據本公司於2027年3月31日或之前發出通知至行政代理，並符合特定淨收入要求（稱為「額外承諾金額」）。於關閉日，本公司完成初始承諾金額，扣除支付給貸款人或代表貸款人的費用及支出。同時於初始承諾金額關閉時，本公司已償還所有先前信貸協議下的義務及承諾（除已發行的認股權證外）（稱為「重組交易」）[1]。
此層次的債務可能對未來營運產生重大影響，包括增加本公司對不利經濟與產業條件的脆弱性，並限制本公司在規劃或應對業務及競爭市場變動時的靈活性。
本公司能否按期支付利息，取決於未來表現，而未來表現受利率風險以及經濟、財務、競爭及其他因素影響，這些因素超出本公司控制範圍。本公司面臨債務利率上漲的風險，這可能導致借款成本上升，影響本公司流動性。本公司未來可能無法產生足夠的營運現金流以現金償還債務，同時進行必要的資本支出。此外，若本公司淨收入未達成Perceptive 信貸協議中所規定的特定金額，則本公司將違反Perceptive 信貸協議。
